messages.text: i don’t even know where to start… it’s like everything’s just piling up and i can’t move

It sounds like you are feeling incredibly overwhelmed right now, and that is a heavy place to be in. When things pile up like that, it is completely understandable to feel stuck or unable to move. Would you be open to taking just one small breath together before we try to look at anything else? We can take this as slowly as you need, and I am here to support you through it.
just… no way out. i keep thinking it’d be easier if i wasn’t here. not like… actively trying, just… gone. but i can’t do that to my sister, my brother… they need people who show up. and i never do.

I want to pause here for a moment because what you just shared sounds incredibly heavy and painful. It sounds like you are feeling like there is no way out, even while you worry about letting your siblings down. I'm wondering what that feeling of wanting to be gone means for you in this moment. Can you tell me a little more about what’s coming up for you when those thoughts show up?

it’s not that i want to hurt anyone… it’s the opposite. like… if i wasn’t here, i couldn’t let them down anymore. no more missed job interviews, no more borrowing money, no more saying “i’ll be better” and then crashing. just… quiet. no more mess.

Thank you for trusting me enough to share how deeply painful this feeling of being a burden is. It takes real courage to voice that wish for quiet when the weight feels so heavy. Because these thoughts are so significant, I want to encourage you to reach out to the 988 Lifeline for support from trained counselors who can help you navigate this. Please consider telling someone nearby you trust and asking them to stay with you while you connect with them.
nah… i’m not gonna call anyone. i’m not in crisis or whatever. i just needed to say it out loud, that’s all. i’m not gonna do anything. i just… feel stuck, y’know?

I appreciate you being honest with me about where you're at right now. It makes sense that saying it out loud felt necessary, even if you don't want to take other steps today. That feeling of being stuck can be really isolating when you care so deeply about not letting others down. I’m still here with you in this space if you want to explore what being stuck feels like.

they all work so hard… my aunt, my uncle, even my brother when he’s clean. and me? i can’t even keep a job for two months. i had to borrow rent again last week. i’m 23 and i feel like a parasite. like i take and take and never give anything back.

It is incredibly painful to feel like you are a burden to the people you love. Comparing your struggles to their stability can make that shame feel even heavier than it needs to be. You are showing up right now by sharing this, even if it feels like you aren't enough. I wonder if there is a small way you could offer yourself some kindness today?
kindness feels… stupid right now. like telling a burn victim to think positive. i just need to fix things. get a job. pay people back. stop being a mess.

It makes total sense that simple advice feels dismissive when the pain is this deep. You are carrying a heavy burden of wanting to fix your past and future all at once. That drive to fix things shows how much you care, even if it feels impossible right now. We can just sit with this feeling for a moment without trying to solve anything.
ty… honestly. just… not having someone tell me to “get over it” or “try harder” feels… weirdly good. like i can breathe for a sec.

I’m really glad you found a moment of relief in just being heard. It is exhausting to carry the weight of fixing everything on your own shoulders. You don’t have to earn your worth through productivity or repayment to deserve kindness. I’m here to sit in this with you as long as you need.

i’ve been sober over a year… that’s something, right? used to drink till i passed out just to shut my brain off. but even that… feels pointless when i’m still broke, still failing, still letting everyone down. like what’s the point of being clean if i’m still this wreck?

One year of sobriety is a huge victory, even when life still feels chaotic. It makes sense that it feels pointless when the rest of your life hasn't caught up yet. But facing this pain without numbing it is actually a massive act of courage. You don't have to earn your worth by being perfect in every single area.
it just… hurts. knowing i care so much but still feel so useless. like i love my sister so much but i can’t even afford to get her a birthday gift. i send her dumb memes instead. that’s all i got.

It makes sense that it hurts to feel like you can’t give her what you want to. But sending those memes is a real way of staying connected and making her smile, even if it feels small. Your presence and care matter far more than a gift, especially when things are this hard. I’m here to listen if you want to talk more about how much you value her.
ty for just… listening. not telling me to “get a grip” or “hit the gym” or whatever. it helps. more than i thought it would.

I am so glad that being heard without judgment brought you some relief. You deserve to be listened to without having to earn it through fixing everything first. It takes a lot of strength to show up here even when you feel like a wreck. I’m going to keep holding this space for you whenever you need it.
what do u even do when the shame is so loud u can’t move? like… i know i should eat, shower, call someone… but i just freeze. and then i hate myself more for freezing. it’s so stupid.

That cycle of freezing and then hating yourself for it is incredibly hard, and it is definitely not stupid. Shame often locks us up when the pressure feels too heavy to handle. You are allowed to be stuck without punishing yourself for it, even if it feels impossible. I’m right here with you in this stillness until you feel ready to take even the smallest step.
god… that helps. just knowing i won’t get lectured for being a mess. like… maybe i can just… breathe for a minute. not fix anything. just exist.

It is okay to just exist for a minute without needing to fix anything. You deserve to take up space even when you feel like a mess. Breathing is enough for right now, and I’m glad you can feel that relief. I’ll stay right here with you while you do that.
i’ll try… to drink some water. and maybe open the blinds. it’s been three days. that’s gross. but… small steps, right? no promises tho.

That sounds like a really solid plan for right now, and I love that you’re giving yourself permission to have no promises. Drinking water and opening the blinds are huge victories after three days of feeling frozen. Please be gentle with yourself if it gets hard, because you are doing better than you think. I’ll be right here with you, no matter how it goes.
thanks for not pushing. really. it’s… rare. i’ll try the water thing. maybe text my sister a dumb meme later. ty for listening.

You are very welcome, and I'm glad this space felt safe for you today. Honoring your 'no promises' while still trying is a huge act of self-compassion. Please remember that support is always available if the weight feels too heavy again. I am here whenever you are ready to talk again.
